summary:
Our project directly addresses the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Dancing with the SARs") by tackling the three fundamental limitations of optical satellite Earth observation: optical blindness caused by persistent cloud cover, wildfire smoke plumes, volcanic ash, and 24-hour polar winter darkness; canopy obstruction that conceals vast sub-canopy floodwaters beneath dense tropical forests; and the steep technical barrier to interpreting raw Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter. 

SARs Unlimited solves these challenges by combining a 144-month (2015–2026) multi-sensor SAR progression atlas, 14 dual-scope phenomenon modes (6 Global and 8 Amazonian), and 15 validated environmental and tectonic crisis events across C-band (5.6 cm), S-band (~12 cm), and NISAR L-band (~24 cm). Users explore surface roughness, dielectric moisture dynamics, and dihedral corner-reflector double-bounce through an interactive split-screen swipe comparator, a real-time radar pixel backscatter (dB) probe, an interactive C/S/L-band forest penetration model, live NASA GIBS/USGS API overlays, and an embedded context-aware local AI scientific assistant. 

This work is critical because it bridges cutting-edge active microwave remote sensing and accessible public decision-making, enabling scientists, disaster responders, and students to monitor hidden flood pulses, deforestation, burn scars, tectonic fault slip, and ice-shelf calving anywhere on Earth regardless of weather or lighting conditions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES:

SARs Unlimited is an offline-first 3D planetary observatory and radar science laboratory. It maps surface deformation, soil moisture, flood inundation, wildfire burn scars, oil spills, and polar ice dynamics from January 2015 through December 2026 across two integrated scales: a Planetary Hydro-Cryosphere Atlas and an Amazon Basin Surface Change Atlas. The application features 14 scientific phenomenon modules, 15 validated crisis events (including the 2017 Larsen C iceberg calving, 2020 Australian Black Summer fires, 2021 Manaus record flood, 2021 La Palma eruption, 2022 Pakistan mega-flood, 2023 Türkiye earthquake InSAR rupture, 2023 Antarctic sea-ice minimum, 2024 Rio Grande do Sul flood, and 2026 NISAR L-band sub-canopy validation), and an 8-stop guided scientific tour.

HOW IT WORKS:

1. 3D Globe & Celestial Engine: Built on CesiumJS, the globe integrates multi-layer optical, topographic (SRTM hillshade), and nighttime lights (VIIRS) basemaps. It features a custom procedural Bortle-1 desert-night skybox with 38 real catalog stars, 2,675 field stars, and a physically rendered Milky Way, alongside custom pole-feathering algorithms that eliminate the typical polar seams at ±85° to ±90°.

2. 144-Month Temporal Engine: Pre-buffers and smoothly animates 288 monthly regional and planetary SAR composite rasters alongside synchronized gauge, precipitation, fire, and backscatter time-series telemetry.

3. Interactive Radar Lab: Features a split-screen swipe comparator with synchronized pan and zoom (1x to 4x), an offscreen 64x64 canvas pixel probe that classifies hovered radar echoes into decibels and physical scattering regimes (specular water, double-bounce trunk reflection, canopy volume loss, basalt roughness, or oil damping), multi-frequency C/S/L-band SVG forest penetration diagrams, and printable scientific incident reports.

4. Extensibility & Local AI: Integrates a local Large Language Model via LM Studio (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) using streaming Electron IPC to inject live globe telemetry into context-aware answers, as well as a universal API loader for live NASA GIBS WMTS feeds, USGS earthquake GeoJSON streams, and the companion BESO47/SARs-Data FastAPI backend.

BENEFITS & GOALS:

The platform democratizes SAR interpretation, demonstrates the unique sub-canopy penetration of NISAR L-band over C-band, provides rapid all-weather disaster assessment tools, and delivers verified, peer-reviewed satellite provenance for research and education.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

- Programming Languages: TypeScript (strict typing for Main, Preload, and Renderer), HTML5/Canvas, CSS3 (glassmorphic theme).

- Desktop Runtime & Framework: Electron (v39), Vite (v7), electron-vite (v5), React 19, and electron-builder.

- Geospatial 3D Engine: CesiumJS (v1.139) with custom offline asset pipeline and Resium bindings.

- Data Visualization & UI: Recharts (v3), Lucide-React icons.

- AI & Backend Services: LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible local REST/SSE endpoint running Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct), Python FastAPI (BESO47/SARs-Data service), and NASA GIBS / USGS REST APIs.

- Operating Systems: Cross-platform desktop support for Windows (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel), and Linux.
